meta.title: Upstream-inspired cycle: workload identity + regressions
meta.battery: NX-RUNAS (process policy run_as_user, upstream #5192) + regressions TV-ENV, TV-LBL, TV-CONC, T4

results.title: Process policy run_as_user
results.desc: Sandbox with ProcessPolicy.run_as_user=nobody; verify exec runs as nobody
results.detail: run_as_user='nobody' rejected (grpc=3): "run_as_user must be 'sandbox' or a numeric UID/GID"; run_as_user='65534' accepted, sandbox Ready, exec id -u -> '1000880000'
results.prose: Upstream #5192 hardened workload identity handling, so I probed the process policy's run_as_user field. The literal username 'nobody' is rejected — validation demands the reserved name 'sandbox' or a numeric UID — but a numeric UID (65534) is accepted and the sandbox runs Ready. Interestingly, commands inside then execute as UID 1000880000, not 65534: on this kubernetes-backed gateway the numeric UID is validated but the platform maps the workload to its own synthetic user namespace identity rather than honoring the raw UID — exactly the kind of identity-invariant gap #5192's deserialize-time enforcement is about.
results.steps: CreateSandbox with SandboxPolicy.process.run_as_user=nobody; wait Ready; ExecSandbox 'id -un'; compare.

results.title: Random payload FS roundtrip
results.desc: Write and re-read random hash within session
results.prose: Wrote this cycle's random SHA-256 payload to /tmp inside the sandbox and read it back from a second exec call — both reads matched. Filesystem continuity within a sandbox lifetime is the baseline the workspace layer builds on.
